round1_to_round2.convergence_verdict: Mostly anchoring on my round-1 file, not independent agreement. All five moved the same way at once (fair values -$15 to -$32, ladder medians -$26 to -$49) with no new evidence between rounds. Each copied my inputs: the CY2027 finviz peer basis, nearly the same 10-12-name peer list, a recurring VPD royalty of $15-20M/qtr around my $20M (agent_4 and agent_5 took $20M exactly), and ~$10/share net cash. Their 1-month ladders are almost a copy of my round-1 ladder_1m (P>=305.61 0.470-0.474 vs my 0.479). Every agent then went below my own round-1 ladder (median $248), because when I asked them to reconcile base scenario with fair value, all five cut the scenario instead of defending it. Independent agreement holds only on the facts I re-verified against primary documents: the fixed-licence schedule, the >30% Q3 guide, share count and cash. The overlap on judgement inputs (VPD run-rate, multiple, peer set) is one source, my file, counted five times.
round1_to_round2.scenario_reconciliation: Ladders match each agent's scenarios. Scenario-weighted means after the 2026-10-06 citation fix: a1 $241, a2 $241, a3 $222, a4 $241, a5 $252. The agents' 12-month ladders were shifted in price by the same proportion as their fair-value changes (a2 177/192 then 172/177, a3 157/158, a4 175/185, a5 158/161, a1 162/166 after the citation gate), giving ladder medians of $192-218. The fair values ($157-175) still do not reconcile with the scenarios: each sits $65-94 below its agent's scenario mean. Every agent states why: the fair value is intrinsic value at a peer-bounded multiple, while the base case is the price the market is expected to pay with part of the premium surviving. That is acceptable only if the fair value is read as value and the ladder as the price forecast.

Interest income is left out of EPS so the cash is not counted twice.
